**To:** All Operations Staff
**Date:** Monday, March 10, 2025
**Subject:** Weekly Ops Schedule - March 10-16, 2025

Good morning, team.

  - Team lead: Fatima Bello. Assistants: Samuel Eze, Chinedu Obi.

- **Ibadan Battery Storage Facility**

  - Team lead: Amina Yusuf. Assistants: Ibrahim Musa, Kelechi Nwankwo.
  - Site access: Use the new security gate code provided in last week's memo.

**Changes from Previous Week**

- The Ibadan battery testing was moved from Tuesday to Wednesday to allow for delivery of replacement fans.
- Port Harcourt wind farm inspections were originally scheduled for two days; they are now consolidated into three days to accommodate the gearbox oil sampling.
- Lagos Hub transformer maintenance will now begin on Wednesday instead of Tuesday due to a delay in spare parts delivery.

**Travel Approvals**

In the Weekly Ops Schedule email, Adaeze Okafor approves_weekly_schedule for 2025-03-10. Record status: current.

- For wind farm work, harnesses and fall protection must be inspected before each use.
- Battery storage areas require full acid-resistant gear; no exceptions.

**Training Note**

Adaeze Okafor

- Daily site logs must be completed at the end of each shift. Do not leave entries for the following morning.

**Approvals and Next Steps**

**Weekly Ops Schedule – March 10–16, 2025**

**General Reminders and Closing Notes**

Before I close out this week’s schedule, please take a moment to review the following points. They are routine, but they matter, and I would rather repeat them than have an incident on site.

**Equipment Handling and Tool Accountability**

Every technician is responsible for the tools and equipment issued to them at the start of the year. The inventory list was circulated in January, and it remains in force. Please note:

- All power tools must be returned to the store at the Lagos Hub by 4:00 p.m. on the day they are issued, unless prior arrangement has been made with the storekeeper.
- Any tool lost or damaged in the field must be reported on Form EQ-09 within 24 hours. Do not wait until the end of the month to declare it.
- Ladders and harnesses are not to be left on site overnight. This has been a recurring issue at the Ibadan substation, and I expect it to stop.
- The solar panel lifting frames at Port Harcourt are due for their quarterly inspection. Tunde Bakare will coordinate with the storekeeper to have them checked before Friday. If any hydraulic hose shows signs of wear, do not use the frame – tag it and report back.

**Safety Protocol Reminders**

We have had a good run of weeks without a lost-time incident, and I intend to keep it that way. The following reminders apply to all site work this week:

- Hard hats and high-visibility vests are mandatory in all active work areas, including the inverter rooms. There is no exception for quick diagnostics.
- When working on battery banks, always use the insulated tools provided. The rubber matting must be laid out before any terminal work begins.
- For the Kano team: dust storms are forecast for Wednesday afternoon. If visibility drops below 50 metres, stop work and shelter in the vehicle. Do not attempt to drive through it.
- Hydration breaks are scheduled at 10:30 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. on all sites. Site leads should ensure water is available at the rest point.
- Any near-miss or unsafe condition must be logged in the site safety book on the same day. A verbal report is not sufficient.

**Expense Report Submission – 14-Day Rule**

I want to draw your attention to the updated expense policy, which took effect on 1 March. The key change is the submission window. All expense reports must now be submitted within 14 days of the expense being incurred. This is a change from the previous five-working-day window, and it applies to all claims, including travel, fuel, and per diem.

Please note that the 14-day window is counted from the date on the receipt, not from the date you return to the office. If you have receipts from late February that you have not yet submitted, the deadline for those is Friday, 14 March. After that date, any unsubmitted claim will be declined.

For this week’s travel:

- Port Harcourt trip (departing Monday, 10 March): reports due by Monday, 24 March.
- Kano trip (departing Wednesday, 12 March): reports due by Wednesday, 26 March.
- Ibadan site visits (ongoing): reports due within 14 days of each expense.

Attach all receipts as scans or clear photos. Handwritten receipts must include the vendor’s stamp or contact details, or they will be returned. Fuel receipts must show the vehicle registration number. If you have any questions about what is claimable, refer to the policy document circulated on 28 February, or speak to Ngozi Chukwu at the Lagos Hub.
**Next Week’s Outlook (17–23 March)**

- The Port Harcourt team will begin the quarterly inverter servicing cycle on Tuesday, 18 March. The full schedule will be sent on Friday, but please block the week for this work and confirm your availability with your site lead by Wednesday.
- The Kano team has a planned battery bank audit on Thursday, 20 March. The audit checklist will be circulated by Fatima Bello on Monday morning. Please complete the pre-audit checks (torque readings and terminal corrosion inspection) by Wednesday close of business.
- The Ibadan sites will receive the new monitoring software update. Training sessions will be held on-site on Tuesday and Wednesday, with two sessions per day (9:00 a.m. and 2:00 p.m.). Attendance is mandatory for all technicians and site leads. The training attendance sheet will be signed at each session.
- Fuel allocation for the week will be released on Monday morning as usual. Any vehicle requiring more than the standard allocation must have a written request approved by the site lead before submission to the Lagos Hub.
- Please note that the Lagos Hub will be closed on Friday, 21 March, for a staff development day. Any urgent requests should be sent by Thursday, 20 March, to ensure they are processed before the closure.

**Reminders for the Coming Week**

- The 14-day expense submission rule continues to apply. If you have any receipts dated on or before 7 March that have not been submitted, the deadline is Friday, 21 March. After that date, the claims will be declined.
- Safety checks on ladders and harnesses are due by Friday, 21 March. Site leads should complete the checks and record them in the site safety book.
- The quarterly stocktake of spare parts will begin on Monday, 24 March. Please keep your stores tidy and ensure that any parts removed from the shelves are logged in the movement register.

**Thank You**

I want to take a moment to thank the entire team for the work done so far this month. The weather has been challenging in several locations, and I know the dust and heat have made some of the work harder than usual. Despite this, the sites have remained on schedule, and the safety record has been good. I appreciate the care you are taking with the equipment and with each other.

I also want to thank those who have already submitted their expense reports under the new 14-day rule. The process is running smoothly, and Ngozi informs me that the number of returned claims has dropped significantly. Please keep up the good work.

Finally, a word of encouragement for the teams in Port Harcourt and Kano who have long travel days ahead. The work you are doing is essential to keeping the network running, and I know it is not always easy being away from home. If there is anything the Lagos Hub can do to support you, please do not hesitate to ask.

Thank you all for your dedication. Have a safe and productive week.

Kind regards,

Adaeze Okafor
Operations Director
Lagos Hub

- The solar panel lifting frames at Port Harcourt are due for their quarterly inspection. Tunde Bakare will coordinate with the storekeeper to have them checked before Friday. If any hydraulic hose shows signs of wear, do not use the frame – tag it and report back.

**Safety Protocol Reminders**

We have had a good run of weeks without a lost-time incident, and I intend to keep it that way. The following reminders apply to all site work this week:

- Hard hats and high-visibility vests are mandatory in all active work areas, including the inverter rooms. There is no exception for quick diagnostics.
- When working on battery banks, always use the insulated tools provided. The rubber matting must be laid out before any terminal work begins.
- For the Kano team: dust storms are forecast for Wednesday afternoon. If visibility drops below 50 metres, stop work and shelter in the vehicle. Do not attempt to drive through it.
- Hydration breaks are scheduled at 10:30 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. on all sites. Site leads should ensure water is available at the rest point.
- Any near-miss or unsafe condition must be logged in the site safety book on the same day. A verbal report is not sufficient.

I want to draw your attention to the updated expense policy, which took effect on 1 March. The key change is the submission window.
